kickoff.d: Agree goals, roles and ways of working with the whole team.

doc_register.d: List every document the project needs, with owner and due date.

proposal.d: Describe the problem, the solution, benefits, cost and timeline.

charter.t: Write and approve the project charter
charter.d: Record objectives, scope, milestones, budget and the sponsor's approval.

stakeholders.t: Identify stakeholders and set up communication
stakeholders.d: List who is affected and agree how and when they are informed.

requirements.d: Interview users and stakeholders and write the business requirements.

srs.d: Turn business needs into precise functional and non-functional requirements.

wbs_schedule.t: Build the work breakdown structure and schedule
wbs_schedule.d: Break the work into tasks, estimate them and link dependencies.

risk_plan.d: Identify risks, score probability and impact, and plan responses.

budget_plan.d: Split the budget by category and confirm who works on what.

architecture.d: Define components, interfaces, data flows and the deployment view.

tech_design.d: Design modules, data model, APIs and security controls in detail.

impl_plan.d: Plan the build sequence, environments, releases and responsibilities.

test_strategy.d: Define test levels, test cases, tools, environments and exit criteria.

env_setup.t: Set up development environment and CI/CD
env_setup.d: Prepare repositories, environments and the automatic build pipeline.

integration.d: Connect the parts into one working system and fix interface issues.

user_manual.d: Explain step by step how users work with the system.

functional_tests.d: Run the test cases and log every defect found.

uat.d: Real users confirm the system meets their needs.

fix_defects.d: Correct the defects found in testing and verify the fixes.

deploy_guide.d: Document installation, configuration, checks and rollback steps.

go_live.d: Release the system to production following the deployment guide.

training.d: Train users and support staff and hand over operations.

closure_report.d: Summarise results against objectives, budget and schedule.

lessons.d: Capture what went well and what to improve next time.

ux_design.d: Design screens and user flows and test them with users.

backend.d: Build the business logic, APIs and authentication.

frontend.d: Build the web pages and connect them to the APIs.

database.d: Create the database schema, migrations and seed data.

performance.d: Check response times and behaviour under expected load.

threat_model.d: Map assets, threats and attack paths and choose controls.

siem.t: Deploy the SIEM and log collection
siem.d: Install the SIEM and connect log sources and agents.

detection.d: Create correlation rules and alerts for the main threats.

incident.d: Write step-by-step playbooks for the most likely incidents.

pentest.d: Attack the system in a controlled way and fix what is found.

data_strategy.d: Decide which data is needed, where it comes from and how it is labelled.

data_pipeline.d: Collect, clean and prepare the data for training.

model_training.d: Train candidate models and tune them on validation data.

model_serving.d: Serve the model through an API and monitor its accuracy.

model_eval.d: Measure accuracy, robustness and fairness before release.

landing_zone.t: Cloud landing zone and network design
landing_zone.d: Design accounts, networks, identities and guardrails.

iac.d: Describe the infrastructure in code (e.g. Terraform) and automate it.

migration.d: Move applications and data to the cloud wave by wave.

observability.d: Set up dashboards, alerts, logs and automatic backups.

dr_test.d: Prove the system can be restored within the agreed time.

mobile_ux.d: Design the app screens and test the prototype with users.

mobile_app.t: Develop the Android and iOS app
mobile_app.d: Build the app screens, navigation and offline behaviour.

mobile_api.d: Build the server API, accounts and notifications.

store_prep.d: Prepare icons, screenshots, descriptions and privacy forms.

device_tests.d: Test on different phones, screen sizes and OS versions.

data_model.d: Map source systems and design the target data model.

etl.d: Extract, transform and load data on a schedule.

warehouse.d: Create the warehouse, schemas, access rights and costs controls.

dashboards.d: Create the dashboards and KPIs the business asked for.

data_quality.d: Check completeness, accuracy and freshness of the data.

solution_design.d: Design how the solution will meet the requirements.

build_core.d: Produce the main deliverables of the project.

internal_review.d: Review the deliverables against the requirements.

pilot.d: Run a small pilot and collect feedback before full rollout.

scope_creep.t: Scope creep: new requests keep being added
scope_creep.m: Freeze scope after the plan milestone; every change goes through a change request with impact on time and cost.

schedule_delay.m: Track progress weekly, protect the critical path and keep a time buffer before go-live.

budget_overrun.m: Compare actual vs planned spending every week; act when CPI drops below 0.95; keep the contingency reserve.

key_person.t: A key team member becomes unavailable
key_person.m: Share knowledge in pairs, document decisions and name a backup for each role.

unclear_requirements.t: Requirements are unclear or change late
unclear_requirements.m: Validate requirements with users early using prototypes and get written sign-off.

integration_issues.m: Agree interfaces early, integrate continuously and test end-to-end every week.

data_protection.t: Personal data is exposed or mishandled (GDPR)
data_protection.m: Apply privacy by design, encrypt data, restrict access and run a data-protection impact assessment.

vendor_delay.t: A supplier or licence arrives late
vendor_delay.m: Order early, follow up weekly and identify an alternative supplier.

tech_debt.m: Code reviews, automated tests and time reserved for refactoring in each sprint.

performance.t: The system is too slow under real load
performance.m: Set performance targets early and load-test before go-live.

false_positives.t: Too many false alerts overwhelm analysts
false_positives.m: Tune rules with real data, add whitelists and measure alert precision weekly.

log_gaps.m: Keep a log-source inventory and check coverage against the threat model.

data_quality.t: Data is incomplete or of poor quality
data_quality.m: Profile the data early, add validation checks and fix problems at the source.

model_bias.t: The model is biased or unfair
model_bias.m: Test performance per group, balance training data and document model limits.

cost_spike.t: Cloud costs grow faster than expected
cost_spike.m: Set budgets and alerts, tag resources and review costs every week.

migration_downtime.m: Migrate in waves, rehearse each cutover and keep a tested rollback plan.

store_rejection.t: The app store rejects the app
store_rejection.m: Follow store guidelines, prepare privacy forms and submit a beta early.

device_fragmentation.t: The app breaks on some devices
device_fragmentation.m: Test on a device matrix covering the most used phones and OS versions.

source_changes.m: Agree data contracts with source owners and monitor schema changes.

stakeholder_availability.t: Stakeholders are not available for decisions
stakeholder_availability.m: Book decision meetings in advance and agree response times.

quality_issues.t: Deliverables do not meet quality expectations
quality_issues.m: Agree acceptance criteria early and review deliverables before hand-over.

p.register_purpose: This register lists every document the project “{project}” needs, who owns it, when it is due and its current status. It is updated as the project progresses.
p.charter_purpose: This charter formally starts the project “{project}”. It sets the objectives, scope, milestones, budget ({budget}) and team, and gives the project manager ({pm}) the authority to use resources.
p.proposal_summary: We propose the project “{project}” ({type}). It will run from {start} to {end} with a team of {team} and a budget of {budget}. The plan contains {tasks} tasks in seven phases.

problem.software: Today the work is done with manual steps and scattered tools, which causes delays, errors and little visibility for managers.
problem.cybersecurity: Attacks and fraud are getting faster and harder to spot. Without central monitoring and automatic detection, threats are found too late and losses grow.
problem.ai_ml: Decisions are made manually from large amounts of data. This is slow, inconsistent and does not scale.
problem.cloud: The current infrastructure is costly to run, slow to change and hard to scale or recover after failures.
problem.mobile: Users expect to do this task from their phone, quickly and at any time. Today they cannot.
problem.data: Data sits in separate systems. Reports are built by hand, are late and do not match each other.
problem.generic: The organisation needs this result to reach its goals, and today it is not available.

p.solution: The project delivers a solution with the following capabilities:
p.brd_purpose: This document describes what the business needs from the project “{project}”, so that the solution can be designed and its success measured.
p.srs_intro: This specification defines the functional and non-functional requirements of “{project}”. It is the reference for design, development and testing.
p.srs_overall: The system ({type}) serves the users and administrators described below. It must be secure, reliable and easy to use, and it is delivered by {end}.
p.tdd_intro: This document explains how “{project}” will be built: components, data, security and the main technical decisions.

design.software: The solution is a web application with a separate API layer and a relational database. Users work in the browser; all access goes through authenticated API calls.
design.cybersecurity: The solution collects logs from all sources into a SIEM, correlates events with detection rules, and gives analysts one console to investigate and respond, supported by automated playbooks.
design.ai_ml: The solution has a data pipeline, a training environment with experiment tracking, a model-serving API and monitoring that triggers retraining when quality drops.
design.cloud: The target is a secure cloud landing zone. Workloads move in waves, run on managed compute and storage, and are fully monitored and backed up.
design.mobile: The solution is a cross-platform mobile app with offline storage, a backend API and a push-notification service, plus an admin portal.
design.data: Data flows from the sources through scheduled ETL pipelines into a central warehouse, where a semantic layer feeds dashboards and reports.
design.generic: The solution is delivered in iterations, each one reviewed with stakeholders before the next starts.

p.sad_intro: This document describes the architecture of “{project}”: its components, how they communicate, where they run, and the quality attributes they must meet.
p.wbs_purpose: The work breakdown structure divides “{project}” into {tasks} tasks across seven phases, from initiation to closure, with owners, dates and deliverables.
p.impl_purpose: This plan explains how “{project}” is built and rolled out between {start} and {end}.
p.impl_approach: Work follows seven phases. Each phase ends with a milestone that must be approved before the next begins. Progress is tracked weekly and reported to stakeholders.
p.test_purpose: This plan defines how the quality of “{project}” will be checked: test levels, test cases, environments, responsibilities and exit criteria.
p.risk_purpose: This assessment identifies the risks of “{project}”, scores them by probability and impact (1–5 each), and defines an owner and a response for each one.
p.deploy_purpose: This guide explains how to install, configure, verify and, if needed, roll back “{project}” in production.
p.manual_intro: This manual explains how to use “{project}”. It is written for everyday users; no technical knowledge is needed.
p.manual_support: For help, contact the project team. The project manager is {pm}.
p.closure_summary: The project “{project}” ran from {start} to {end}. It reached {progress} completion. This report compares the results with the plan, records lessons learned and confirms the hand-over.
